issues.description: Predicate `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` is correct but unreadable; the invariant deserves a literate comment
issues.detail: The intent — 'a bare @layer statement (no block) is allowed before @import per the CSS cascade-layers spec, but a @layer with a block is not' — is not stated anywhere. A reader has to reverse-engineer the spec from the negated conjunction. A one-line comment naming the invariant (`@layer name;` is statement-form and permitted before @import; `@layer name { ... }` is a block-form rule and is not) plus a link to the relevant CSS spec section would make the predicate self-explanatory and prevent future regressions in the opposite direction. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: Prefer a presence check over `typeof === 'undefined'` for postcss node detection
issues.detail: PostCSS sets `node.nodes` to an array on container at-rules and leaves it absent on statement at-rules. The idiomatic and slightly more robust test is `node.nodes == null` or simply `!node.nodes` (also handles the theoretical case of `null`). `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` works but is wordier and asymmetric with how the rest of the file inspects nodes. A minor readability nit, not a correctness issue.

issues.description: Test coverage for the positive case (bare `@layer foo;` before `@import`) should be asserted alongside the new negative case
issues.detail: The diff adds the failing case `@layer foo {}` before `@import` (good — it pins the new behavior). But the symmetric positive case — `@layer foo;` followed by `@import url(...)` should remain accepted — guards against the opposite regression where someone later 'simplifies' the predicate back to `nodeName !== 'layer'` or, worse, removes the layer exception entirely. If there is already an accept-case in the existing test file for statement-form @layer, this is moot; if not, add one. A small investment that pays interest forever.

review.summary: RIGOROUS on the algorithm and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the explanation. The fix is correct: per the CSS cascade-layers spec, statement-form `@layer name;` is permitted before `@import` while block-form `@layer name { ... }` is a regular rule that disqualifies a subsequent `@import` from the leading-import position. Distinguishing the two by presence of `node.nodes` is the right invariant and matches how PostCSS models container vs. leaf at-rules; complexity is unchanged (single linear scan, O(n) over preceding siblings). The two concrete improvements are stylistic and cheap: write down the invariant in a comment so the next reader doesn't have to reconstruct it from the negated conjunction, and consider `!node.nodes` over `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'`. Worth also asserting the positive symmetric case (`@layer foo;` before `@import` remains valid) if it isn't already covered, so the predicate is pinned from both sides.
